newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Waigel-latest data do not alter deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-latest data do not alter deficit forecast.

text.p: German finance minister Theo Waigel said on Monday no recent economic data gave any reason to alter a German government forecast of a budget deficit at 2.9 percent of gross domestic product by the end of the year.
"The latest economic data do not give any reason to change the government deficit forecast," Waigel told journalists in Brussels, where he was attending a meeting of European Union finance ministers.
Waigel reaffirmed that Germany's aim was to ensure it met the criteria for entry into monetary union. A budget deficit of three percent of GDP or lower is one such criterion.
Waigel also said that several European Union ministers had specifically acknowledged to him the burden of German unification in its efforts to meet the criteria.
